title: Uniform noise stability of linear thresholds
statement: The family of linear threshold classes is uniformly noise-stable: every function in the family is $\pm 1$-valued, and there exists a function $\varepsilon:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $0\leq\varepsilon(\delta)\leq1$ for $0\leq\delta\leq\tfrac12$, with $\varepsilon(\delta)\to0$ as $\delta\to0^+$. For every dimension $n$, every function $f$ in the linear threshold class on $\{0,1\}^n$, and every $0<\delta\leq\tfrac12$, its noise sensitivity satisfies $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)\leq\varepsilon(\delta)$, where $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)=(1-\operatorname{Stab}_{1-2\delta}(f))/2$ and stability is computed using the uniform measure on the Boolean cube.
hypotheses_covered: all members of the class in every natural dimension are $\pm1$-valued
$\varepsilon(\delta)$ tends to zero as $\delta$ approaches zero from above
the noise sensitivity bound holds for every dimension, every class member, and $0<\delta\leq1/2$
replaced:
The family of linear threshold functions on Boolean cubes is uniformly noise-stable: every function has the form $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(c+\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i(-1)^{x_i})$ for real coefficients, is $\{-1,1\}$-valued, and there exists $\varepsilon:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $0\leq\varepsilon(\delta)\leq1$ on $[0,1/2]$, $\lim_{\delta\to0^{+}}\varepsilon(\delta)=0$ and
\[
\Pr[f(X)\neq f(Y)]\leq\varepsilon(\delta)
\]
for every dimension $n\in\mathbb N$, every such $f$ and every $0<\delta\leq1/2$.
Here $\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(t)=1$ for $t\geq0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$, $X$ is uniform on $\{0,1\}^{n}$, and $Y$ independently flips its coordinates with probability $\delta$.
